tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the weekly program?

options.A: It enables people to earn more money.
options.B: It teaches the importance of financing.
options.C: It helps people with budgeting.
options.D: It introduces a novel way to invest.

questions.cn: 关于这档周播节目，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.D: 它介绍一种新颖的投资方式。

questions.stem: What did the man read recently?

options.A: Many Americans are not satisfied with their income.
options.B: Many Americans have no idea about how to invest.
options.C: Most Americans do not know how to save money.
options.D: Most Americans do not stick to a budget.

questions.cn: 男士最近读到了什么？

optionsCn.A: 许多美国人对自己的收入不满意。
optionsCn.B: 许多美国人不知道怎么投资。
optionsCn.C: 大多数美国人不知道怎么存钱。
optionsCn.D: 大多数美国人不按预算花钱。

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do first to avoid getting into debt?

options.A: Keep track of his money.
options.B: Live within his means.
options.C: Find more sources of income.
options.D: Refrain from buying luxuries.

questions.cn: 为避免陷入债务，女士建议男士首先做什么？

optionsCn.D: 不买奢侈品。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about online shopping?

options.A: It offers a greater variety of items.
options.B: It helps avoid unnecessary spending.
options.C: It changes one's way of living.
options.D: It saves one's time for shopping.

questions.cn: 关于网购，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它提供更多种类的商品。
optionsCn.B: 它有助于避免不必要的花费。
optionsCn.D: 它节省人的购物时间。

lines.t: M: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money.
lines.cn: M：欢迎收听《理财要务》，一档帮你管理钱财的周播节目。

lines.t: M: Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting.
lines.cn: M：今晚我要和玛丽·约翰逊聊预算。

lines.t: F: Hello, everyone.
lines.cn: F：大家好。

lines.t: F: There's a magic about money.
lines.cn: F：钱有一种魔力。

lines.t: F: When it's not planned for, tracked, and kept a record of, it literally disappears.
lines.cn: F：如果不做计划、不跟踪、不记账，它真的会凭空消失。

lines.t: M: What are some of the steps we can take to prevent this from happening?
lines.cn: M：我们可以采取哪些步骤来防止这种情况？

lines.t: F: Well, it's all about keeping track of your money.
lines.cn: F：嗯，关键就是跟踪你的钱。

lines.t: F: If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them.
lines.cn: F：如果不这么做，你永远无法为预算设定目标，也没有坚持目标的纪律。

lines.t: M: That's easier said than done.
lines.cn: M：说起来容易做起来难。

lines.t: M: I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget.
lines.cn: M：我最近读到，只有 41% 的美国人按预算花钱。

lines.t: F: Yes, but knowing what you earn and what you spend can give you reassurance that you won't get into debt in the first place.
lines.cn: F：是的，但知道自己挣多少、花多少，能让你安心，确信自己一开始就不会陷入债务。

lines.t: F: You can do this by adding up all of your sources of income you have and writing them all down on a piece of paper.
lines.cn: F：你可以把所有收入来源加总，写在一张纸上。

lines.t: F: On the same page, write down all of your monthly expenses.
lines.cn: F：在同一页上，写下你所有的月度开支。

lines.t: M: I'm always amazed at how much my expenses add up, but designating each item as an income or an expense really helps me have a much better sense of all my spending.
lines.cn: M：我的开支总和总让我吃惊，但把每一项标为收入或支出，确实帮我更好地了解自己的所有花费。

lines.t: F: Right.
lines.cn: F：对。

lines.t: F: Most people have no idea how much they spend each day, let alone each week or month, no matter how careful they are.
lines.cn: F：大多数人根本不知道自己每天花多少，更别说每周或每月，无论他们多么小心。

lines.t: F: Next, subtract your monthly expenses from income.
lines.cn: F：接下来，用收入减去月度开支。

lines.t: F: If the result is positive, you are living within your means.
lines.cn: F：如果结果是正数，说明你量入为出。

lines.t: F: If the result is a negative number, you're going to have to cut back on your spending.
lines.cn: F：如果结果是负数，你就得减少开支了。

lines.t: M: I'm usually a negative number.
lines.cn: M：我通常是负数。

lines.t: M: I just can't resist the allure of all those prestigious goods.
lines.cn: M：我就是抵挡不住那些名牌货的诱惑。

lines.t: F: Well, it's not a catastrophe, but you do have to make some changes.
lines.cn: F：这也不是灾难，但你确实得做些改变。

lines.t: F: Try cutting back on those non-essential items.
lines.cn: F：试着削减那些非必需的东西。

lines.t: F: Sell some stuff in your attic or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate.
lines.cn: F：把阁楼里的东西卖掉，或者上网购物以避开巧克力之类不必要的诱惑。

lines.t: F: Failing that, you can always find yourself a part-time job.
lines.cn: F：如果这些都做不到，你还可以给自己找份兼职。

options.A: It is brand-new.

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Hi there.
lines.cn: M：你好。

lines.t: M: I've come to see the flat.
lines.cn: M：我来看房子。

lines.t: M: My name is Mark Adams.
lines.cn: M：我叫马克·亚当斯。

lines.t: M: We spoke on the phone on Wednesday.
lines.cn: M：我们周三通过电话。

lines.t: F: Hi Mark.
lines.cn: F：你好，马克。

lines.t: F: Come on up.
lines.cn: F：上来吧。

lines.t: F: I'll buzz you in.
lines.cn: F：我给你开门。

lines.t: F: Green door on the second floor, on the right side.
lines.cn: F：二楼右手边，绿色的门。

lines.t: M: Nice to meet you.
lines.cn: M：很高兴见到你。

lines.t: F: I spoke to all your references, and they all checked out okay.
lines.cn: F：我跟你所有的证明人都联系过了，他们都没问题。

lines.t: F: So let me show you around.
lines.cn: F：那我带你看看。

lines.t: F: The place actually belongs to my mother, but her health isn't great, so we finally managed to persuade her to move in with us and rent this old place out.
lines.cn: F：这房子其实是我母亲的，但她身体不好，我们终于说服她搬来和我们一起住，把这老房子租出去。

lines.t: M: It's a great size.
lines.cn: M：面积很好。

lines.t: M: Plenty of space.
lines.cn: M：空间充足。

lines.t: M: Very versatile.
lines.cn: M：非常实用多变。

lines.t: M: I think it's a winner for us.
lines.cn: M：我觉得对我们来说很合适。

lines.t: F: Yes.
lines.cn: F：是的。

lines.t: F: All the appliances are brand new.
lines.cn: F：所有家电都是全新的。

lines.t: F: There's a washing machine and a tumble dryer in the utility room next to the kitchen.
lines.cn: F：厨房旁边的杂物间里有洗衣机和烘干机。

lines.t: F: Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous.
lines.cn: F：衣柜空间也很多，这很棒。

lines.t: M: My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes.
lines.cn: M：我妻子的鞋多得离谱。

lines.t: M: Now, the big question.
lines.cn: M：现在，最重要的问题。

lines.t: M: What about noise and the neighbors?
lines.cn: M：噪音和邻居怎么样？

lines.t: F: Well, all the neighbors are elderly, so no noisy kids, and the back of the house overlooks a clear and peaceful pond.
lines.cn: F：嗯，邻居都是老年人，所以没有吵闹的孩子；房子后面俯瞰一片清澈宁静的池塘。

lines.t: F: So it's perfect if tranquility is what you are looking for.
lines.cn: F：所以如果你想要的是宁静，这里再合适不过。

lines.t: M: That's good news.
lines.cn: M：这真是好消息。

lines.t: M: We've been living in a less than glamorous part of Aberdeen, constantly harassed day and night by noisy neighbors.
lines.cn: M：我们一直住在阿伯丁不太体面的地段，日夜被吵闹的邻居骚扰。

lines.t: M: Getting to work was a nightmare too, as we only have one car, and my wife has to use it, as she works nights at the hospital.
lines.cn: M：上班也是场噩梦，因为我们只有一辆车，而我妻子上夜班，得用车去医院。

lines.t: F: Well, if you like the place, it's yours as soon as I get a contract drawn up with the solicitor.
lines.cn: F：嗯，如果你喜欢这地方，等我和律师把合同拟好，它就是你的了。

lines.t: F: The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory on signing the contract.
lines.cn: F：签合同时必须交第一个月房租和押金。

lines.t: F: Then we can work out when is the best day for you to pay rent each month.
lines.cn: F：然后我们可以商定每月哪一天交房租对你最合适。

lines.t: M: We'll be incredibly happy to be your new tenants.
lines.cn: M：能成为你的新房客，我们会非常高兴。

lines.t: M: Thank you so much.
lines.cn: M：非常感谢。

lines.t: M: My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes.
lines.cn: M：我妻子会很激动能离开现在这个破地方，开始往那些衣柜里塞满她那些鞋子。

questions.stem: What has the new study found about children watching television?

options.A: The more commercials they see, the more brands they get to know.
options.B: The more commercials they see, the more they adore celebrities.
options.C: The more television they watch, the fewer conflicts in the family.
options.D: The more television they watch, the greater their parents' stress.

questions.cn: 关于孩子看电视，这项新研究发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们看到的广告越多，认识的品牌越多。
optionsCn.B: 他们看到的广告越多，越崇拜名人。
optionsCn.C: 他们看电视越多，家庭冲突越少。
optionsCn.D: 他们看电视越多，父母压力越大。

questions.stem: What are parents advised to do to reduce the impact of TV commercials?

options.A: Inform children of the family's financial situation.
options.B: Shift children's attention to interesting activities.
options.C: Involve children in making purchasing decisions.
options.D: Help children understand advertising's intent.

questions.cn: 为减少电视广告的影响，建议父母做什么？

optionsCn.A: 告诉孩子家里的财务状况。
optionsCn.B: 把孩子的注意力转向有趣的活动。
optionsCn.D: 帮孩子理解广告的意图。

questions.stem: What makes children particularly vulnerable to TV commercials?

options.A: Their limited cognitive ability.
options.B: Their strong natural curiosity.
options.C: Their admiration for celebrities.
options.D: Their lack of social experience.

questions.cn: 是什么让孩子特别容易受电视广告影响？

optionsCn.B: 他们强烈的天然好奇心。
optionsCn.D: 他们缺乏社会经验。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels.
lines.cn: 一项新研究发现，孩子看电视的时长与父母压力水平之间呈正相关。

lines.t: Why?
lines.cn: 为什么？

lines.t: Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising.
lines.cn: 因为孩子看电视越多，接触广告就越多。

lines.t: The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store.
lines.cn: 他们看到的广告越多，和父母一起去商店时就越可能坚持要买那些东西。

lines.t: This could generate conflict if the parents refuse.
lines.cn: 如果父母拒绝，就可能产生冲突。

lines.t: All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels.
lines.cn: 研究者说，这一切都会加剧父母的总体压力水平。

lines.t: What's the solution?
lines.cn: 那解决办法是什么？

lines.t: Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time.
lines.cn: 也许最明显的就是减少屏幕时间。

lines.t: Commercial content is there for a reason—to elicit purchasing behavior.
lines.cn: 商业内容的存在是有目的的——引发购买行为。

lines.t: So, parents might want to shut off the TV.
lines.cn: 所以，父母也许想干脆把电视关掉。

lines.t: Researchers concede that this is easier said than done, so they suggest another option.
lines.cn: 研究者承认这说起来容易做起来难，于是他们提出了另一个选择。

lines.t: Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases.
lines.cn: 父母可以改变自己和孩子谈论购物的方式。

lines.t: The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions.
lines.cn: 研究者建议，父母在家庭购物决策上征求孩子的意见。

lines.t: They shouldn't try to control all purchases.
lines.cn: 他们不应试图控制所有购买。

lines.t: Instead, parents might tell their children things like, I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands.
lines.cn: 相反，父母可以这样对孩子说：某些产品或品牌，我会听你的建议。

lines.t: This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands.
lines.cn: 研究者断言，这种沟通方式能让孩子提出更少的购买要求。

lines.t: That means less parent stress.
lines.cn: 这也意味着父母的压力更小。

lines.t: However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television.
lines.cn: 然而，随着电视接触量增加，这种沟通的保护作用会减弱。

lines.t: This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive.
lines.cn: 这是因为针对儿童的广告特别有说服力。

lines.t: Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music, and celebrity endorsements, to appeal to children.
lines.cn: 广告商用各种手法吸引孩子，比如鲜艳的色彩、欢快的音乐和名人代言。

lines.t: Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent.
lines.cn: 此外，孩子还不具备充分理解广告意图的认知能力。

lines.t: That makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements.
lines.cn: 这让他们特别容易受广告影响。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What baffling phenomenon is discussed in the passage?

options.A: Bad guys may do good deeds.
options.B: Bad guys may go unpunished.
options.C: Good guys may not always cooperate.
options.D: Good guys may get unfair treatment.

questions.cn: 文章讨论了什么令人费解的现象？

optionsCn.C: 好人不一定都愿意合作。
optionsCn.D: 好人可能受到不公平对待。

questions.stem: How are we all judged according to the passage?

options.A: By what we do.
options.B: By fair evaluation.
options.C: In comparison with others.
options.D: In accordance with set standards.

questions.cn: 根据文章，我们是如何被评判的？

optionsCn.D: 按照既定标准。

questions.stem: What can a normal person do when faced with people who perform better?

options.A: Learn from them earnestly.
options.B: Compete with them actively.
options.C: Leave them alone temporarily.
options.D: Cooperate with them sincerely.

questions.cn: 面对表现更好的人，一个普通人能做什么？

optionsCn.D: 真诚地与他们合作。

questions.stem: What may discourage people from performing good deeds?

options.A: Being dismissed as hypocritical.
options.B: Not getting the reward they deserve.
options.C: Having to make too many sacrifices.
options.D: Being misunderstood by people around.

questions.cn: 什么可能让人不愿再行善？

optionsCn.D: 被身边的人误解。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Everyone is supposed to cheer for good guys, and we should only punish the bad guys.
lines.cn: 人人都应该为好人喝彩，我们只该惩罚坏人。

lines.t: But that's not what we always do.
lines.cn: 但我们并不总是这么做。

lines.t: Most of the time, we do indeed reward good people.
lines.cn: 大多数时候，我们确实奖励好人。

lines.t: We also often punish people who harm others or who aren't good team players.
lines.cn: 我们也常常惩罚伤害他人的人，或者不善于团队合作的人。

lines.t: But sometimes, the good guys also get punished or criticized.
lines.cn: 但有时，好人也会受到惩罚或批评。

lines.t: Specifically, because they are so good.
lines.cn: 具体来说，正因为他们太好了。

lines.t: This seems baffling, because it's detrimental to group cooperation.
lines.cn: 这看起来令人费解，因为这对群体合作有害。

lines.t: However, the phenomenon has been discovered in multiple fields, and it has been found in every society.
lines.cn: 然而，这一现象已在多个领域被发现，而且在每个社会都被观察到。

lines.t: Why does this happen?
lines.cn: 为什么会这样？

lines.t: Research suggests a simple reason.
lines.cn: 研究给出了一个简单的原因。

lines.t: When one person looks really good, others look bad by comparison.
lines.cn: 当一个人看起来非常出色时，相比之下别人就显得差。

lines.t: Those others then have an incentive in stopping that person from looking good.
lines.cn: 于是那些人就有动机去阻止这个人显得出色。

lines.t: Especially if they can't or won't compete.
lines.cn: 尤其当他们无法或不愿竞争时。

lines.t: After all, we're all judged in comparison with others.
lines.cn: 毕竟，我们都是在与他人比较中被评判的。

lines.t: When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do?
lines.cn: 面对更优秀的人时，一个普通人能做什么？

lines.t: One option is to actively compete.
lines.cn: 一种选择是积极竞争。

lines.t: A second option is to bring that person down.
lines.cn: 第二种选择是把那个人拉下来。

lines.t: That is, to suppress their cooperation or work ethic, infer selfish motives for their actions, or imply real or imagined hypocrisy.
lines.cn: 也就是压制他们的合作精神或职业操守，把他们的行为推断为自私动机，或暗示他们真实存在或想象中的虚伪。

lines.t: Other tactics include attacking them on unrelated dimensions or punishing them outright.
lines.cn: 其他手段包括在不相关的方面攻击他们，或干脆惩罚他们。

lines.t: Why does this matter?
lines.cn: 这为什么重要？

lines.t: Critics often attack the motives of people who protect the environment, donate money, or work too hard.
lines.cn: 批评者常常攻击那些保护环境、捐款或工作过于努力的人的动机。

lines.t: Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds.
lines.cn: 这些善举被那些自己不做这些事的人斥为幼稚或虚伪。

lines.t: This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds.
lines.cn: 这种批评最终可能会让人不愿再行善。

lines.t: So it's important to recognize these attacks for what they are.
lines.cn: 所以，认清这些攻击的本质很重要。

questions.stem: What do children do when they reach late adolescence?

options.A: They prioritize romance over friendship.
options.B: They try to strengthen same-sex friendships.
options.C: They begin to take friendship more seriously.
options.D: They compete intensely for romantic partners.

questions.cn: 孩子到了青春后期会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们把恋爱置于友谊之上。
optionsCn.B: 他们努力加强同性友谊。
optionsCn.C: 他们开始更认真地对待友谊。
optionsCn.D: 他们为争夺恋人激烈竞争。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills, and rewarded for different acts.
lines.cn: 在美国，大多数研究者承认，男孩和女孩被以不同的方式养育，被教授不同的技能，因不同的行为而受到奖励。

lines.t: Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others.
lines.cn: 人们一致认为，女性擅长某些任务，男性擅长另一些。

lines.t: There is little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other.
lines.cn: 很少有人否认，某些人格特质在一性中比在另一性中更为突出。

lines.t: All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days.
lines.cn: 尽管如此，性别差异近来在媒体上仍是热门话题。

lines.t: Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny.
lines.cn: 自妇女运动兴起以来，性别角色行为受到了更细致的审视。

lines.t: How has this affected friendship?
lines.cn: 这对友谊产生了什么影响？

lines.t: How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations?
lines.cn: 两性在友谊关系中有何不同？

lines.t: Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age.
lines.cn: 大多数青春期前的孩子都有一个最好的朋友，通常是同性别、年龄相仿的人。

lines.t: Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships.
lines.cn: 两性对这些童年友谊的回忆本质上都是正面的。

lines.t: They do not differ in this respect.
lines.cn: 在这一点上他们并无差别。

lines.t: However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come.
lines.cn: 然而，这些早期友谊中所进行的游戏类型，预示了日后将要出现的差异。

lines.t: Boys tend to form playgroups that are competitive in nature.
lines.cn: 男孩倾向于形成具有竞争性的游戏群体。

lines.t: Girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises.
lines.cn: 女孩的群体则更多围绕合作性活动。

lines.t: Thus, at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning, while girls, by contrast, play house and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.
lines.cn: 因此，男孩在很小的时候就变得在意努力竞争和取胜，而女孩则相反，玩过家家和上学游戏，扮演需要彼此支持的角色。

lines.t: Speaking of their childhood, men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender role opinions of other boys.
lines.cn: 谈到童年，男性回忆说，他们对其他男孩的性别角色看法反应强烈且十分在意。

lines.t: Girls in preteen years appear to be less susceptible to gender role pressure.
lines.cn: 青春期前的女孩似乎对性别角色压力不那么敏感。

lines.t: It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior.
lines.cn: 直到开始约会的年纪，女性才报告说在意女性化的行为。

lines.t: Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age.
lines.cn: 而男性几乎在任何年纪，只要有人说他们的行为不够男性化，都会有反应。

lines.t: These early attitudes, reinforced by social conditioning, continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence.
lines.cn: 这些早期态度经社会教化强化后，在青春期继续在两性的友谊中发挥积极作用。

lines.t: This is a period when the majority of males once again report a close alliance with same-sex friends.
lines.cn: 这一时期，大多数男性再次报告与同性朋友关系紧密。

lines.t: Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship.
lines.cn: 但此时，竞争更为激烈，大量精力被投入到争夺地位上，一股明确的竞争暗流渗透在关系之中。

lines.t: Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age.
lines.cn: 女性虽方式不同，但这个年纪也同样拥有脆弱的关系。

lines.t: For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement.
lines.cn: 对她们来说，忠诚的纽带只延伸到恋爱关系的那条界线。

lines.t: This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence, when dating and relationships with boys take sharp precedence over sisterhood.
lines.cn: 这在青春后期最为常见，那时约会和与男孩的关系明显优先于姐妹情谊。

lines.t: Actually, dating dilutes the intensity of same-sex friendships for men also.
lines.cn: 事实上，约会同样稀释了男性同性友谊的强度。

lines.t: For the majority of us, the moment we begin to date seriously, there's a competition between romance and friendship.
lines.cn: 对我们大多数人来说，一旦开始认真约会，恋爱与友谊之间就会出现竞争。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why do disabled job applicants feel reluctant to disclose their disability information?

options.A: They regard it as a matter of sheer privacy.
options.B: They are worried about being turned down.
options.C: They fear that their condition will be made widely known.
options.D: They are afraid to be discriminated against once recruited.

questions.cn: 残疾求职者为什么不愿披露自己的残疾信息？

optionsCn.A: 他们认为这纯属隐私问题。
optionsCn.C: 他们害怕自己的病情被广泛知晓。
optionsCn.D: 他们害怕入职后受到歧视。

questions.stem: When does the speaker suggest applicants reveal their disability information?

options.A: After receiving a job offer.
options.B: During a job interview.
options.C: When confirming an interview.
options.D: Upon completing a cover letter.

questions.cn: 讲话者建议求职者何时透露残疾信息？

optionsCn.D: 写完求职信时。

questions.stem: What are people advised to do when filling out their job application form?

options.A: Describe the true state of their health.
options.B: Provide all the information required.
options.C: Stress the irrelevance of their disability to the job.
options.D: Avoid mentioning the name of their disability.

questions.cn: 填写求职申请表时，建议人们怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 如实描述他们的健康状况。
optionsCn.C: 强调其残疾与工作无关。
optionsCn.D: 避免提及所患残疾的名称。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Good afternoon!
lines.cn: 下午好！

lines.t: In today's lecture, we'll be talking about how and when to disclose a disability when applying for a job.
lines.cn: 在今天这堂课里，我们要谈的是求职时如何以及何时披露残疾。

lines.t: On average, about 20% of the population has some form of disability.
lines.cn: 平均而言，约 20% 的人口患有某种形式的残疾。

lines.t: Most countries these days have equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws.
lines.cn: 如今大多数国家都有机会平等和反歧视的法律。

lines.t: Yet, disabled people often find it hard to decide when, how, and if at all, to raise their disability problem with a potential employer.
lines.cn: 然而，残障人士常常难以决定何时、如何、甚至是否向潜在雇主提出自己的残疾问题。

lines.t: There is uncertainty about how a recruiter will perceive their disability.
lines.cn: 招聘者会如何看待他们的残疾，存在不确定性。

lines.t: As such, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position as a result of disclosing this personal information.
lines.cn: 因此，许多求职者担心，一旦披露这一个人信息，自己就不会被考虑录用。

lines.t: And research has validated this as a genuine concern for many job applicants.
lines.cn: 研究已证实，这是许多求职者真实存在的顾虑。

lines.t: It's a natural reaction, but it shouldn't be a reason to stay quiet.
lines.cn: 这是自然的反应，但它不该成为保持沉默的理由。

lines.t: People need to remember that they are applying for a position they have the skills and experience to excel in.
lines.cn: 人们需要记住，他们申请的是一个自己有能力、有经验做出成绩的职位。

lines.t: Discussing a disability with a potential employer may help them make reasonable workplace adjustments in their favor.
lines.cn: 与潜在雇主讨论残疾情况，可能有助于雇主为他们做出合理的工作场所调整。

lines.t: It's most appropriate to discuss a disability when they reply to confirm an interview.
lines.cn: 最合适的讨论时机，是在回复确认面试的时候。

lines.t: This information needn't be put up front in their cover letter or resume because it's probably not relevant to the position itself.
lines.cn: 这些信息不必写在求职信或简历前面，因为它可能与职位本身并不相关。

lines.t: Candidates with disabilities should feel they have the power to make their own decisions around sharing this information free from prejudice.
lines.cn: 有残疾的求职者应当觉得自己有权在不受偏见影响的情况下，自主决定是否分享这一信息。

lines.t: If they find an organization that doesn't celebrate diversity and inclusion, it could say a lot about the company's culture.
lines.cn: 如果他们发现某个组织并不推崇多元与包容，这本身就足以说明公司文化。

lines.t: Perhaps the organization isn't the right fit.
lines.cn: 也许这个组织并不适合自己。

lines.t: It's important for them to remember that they are seeking a manager and employer that's going to be supportive and continue to give them a great employment experience.
lines.cn: 他们必须记住，自己寻找的是愿意支持他们、并持续给予良好工作体验的管理者和雇主。

lines.t: Companies sometimes offer candidates the chance to disclose disabilities on their application form.
lines.cn: 公司有时会在申请表上给求职者披露残疾的机会。

lines.t: But people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing.
lines.cn: 但人们不该觉得受这种方式或时机所限。

lines.t: People should avoid sharing the name of their disability or condition.
lines.cn: 人们应当避免说出所患残疾或病症的名称。

lines.t: There is always the risk that the recruiter will research information that is inaccurate or irrelevant.
lines.cn: 招聘者总有可能去查证那些不准确或无关的信息。

lines.t: If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when and whether to share this information.
lines.cn: 如果人们认为自己的残疾不会影响其在所招聘职位上的表现，那么完全有权选择何时以及是否分享这一信息。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did some American researchers find about students' reading comprehension in the presence of background noise?

options.A: Their scores were least affected by music with speech.
options.B: It was the poorest when there was background speech.
options.C: Their scores were most depressed with instrumental music.
options.D: It was disrupted by the sound of an air conditioner or fan.

questions.cn: 关于学生在背景噪声下阅读理解的成绩，一些美国研究者发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们的得分受带说话声的音乐影响最小。
optionsCn.B: 在有背景说话声时成绩最差。
optionsCn.C: 他们的得分在器乐下最低。
optionsCn.D: 它被空调或风扇声所干扰。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the British researchers about the degree of interference from background noise?

options.A: It has to do with the type and volume of the background noise.
options.B: It has to do with short-term memory for listening comprehension.
options.C: It depends on the overlap in processing different kinds of information.
options.D: It depends on the participants' ability to concentrate on the task at hand.

questions.cn: 关于背景噪声的干扰程度，我们从英国研究者那里了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它与背景噪声的类型和音量有关。
optionsCn.B: 它与听力理解的短期记忆有关。
optionsCn.C: 它取决于加工不同信息时的重叠程度。
optionsCn.D: 它取决于参与者专注于当前任务的能力。

questions.stem: What is best for students to do when writing essays according to some research?

options.A: Keep everything as quiet as possible.
options.B: Play nothing but instrumental music.
options.C: Use vocal material as little as possible.
options.D: Wear a pair of earphones or headphones.

questions.cn: 根据一些研究，学生写文章时最好怎么做？

optionsCn.D: 戴一副耳塞或耳机。

questions.stem: How do people of different personalities react to distractions according to other studies? That's the end of Listening Comprehension.

options.A: Sociable people were immune to all distractions.
options.B: Shy quiet people were most adversely impacted.
options.C: Less outgoing people were more affected by silence.
options.D: Confident people were unaffected by high-arousal music.

questions.cn: 根据其他研究，不同性格的人对干扰有何反应？

optionsCn.A: 善于交际的人对所有干扰都免疫。
optionsCn.B: 害羞安静的人受负面影响最大。
optionsCn.C: 不太外向的人受安静的影响更大。
optionsCn.D: 自信的人不受高唤醒音乐影响。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Smartphones distract attention and reduce learning because of their potential to offer activities more inviting than study.
lines.cn: 智能手机分散注意力、降低学习效果，因为它们可能提供比学习更吸引人的活动。

lines.t: But what about background sound alone?
lines.cn: 但仅仅是背景声音又会怎样？

lines.t: A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music, or general noise.
lines.cn: 一组美国研究者比较了学生在有背景说话声、器乐或一般噪声的情况下阅读文字材料的理解情况。

lines.t: General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan.
lines.cn: 一般噪声是中性的，比如空调或风扇的声音。

lines.t: Students' scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech.
lines.cn: 在背景说话声下，学生的得分最低。

lines.t: Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech.
lines.cn: 在音乐下的理解成绩略好于在说话声下。

lines.t: However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more.
lines.cn: 然而，当要求他们辨认旋律而不是理解文本时，背景音乐的干扰更大。

lines.t: When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little, if any, hindrance of reading comprehension.
lines.cn: 当背景说话声是参与者不熟悉的语言时，对阅读理解几乎没有妨碍。

lines.t: British researchers compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise, and silence on short-term memory.
lines.cn: 英国研究者比较了背景说话声、带唱音乐、器乐、一般背景噪声和安静对短期记忆的影响。

lines.t: Background speech had the biggest negative effect.
lines.cn: 背景说话声的负面影响最大。

lines.t: Vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental.
lines.cn: 带唱音乐比器乐的干扰略大。

lines.t: In general, background noise and silence were least disruptive.
lines.cn: 总体而言，背景噪声和安静造成的干扰最小。

lines.t: It seems the degree of interference from background noise depends on the overlap between the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise.
lines.cn: 看来背景噪声的干扰程度，取决于任务所需的加工过程与屏蔽背景噪声所需的加工过程之间的重叠程度。

lines.t: The studies suggest that when people read and when they try to remember any verbal material, background speech will inhibit their ability.
lines.cn: 这些研究表明，当人们阅读、以及试图记住任何文字材料时，背景说话声都会妨碍他们的能力。

lines.t: Instrumental music will have, at worst, a slight effect.
lines.cn: 器乐的影响最多也只是轻微的。

lines.t: When students write essays, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.
lines.cn: 然而，当学生写文章时，另一项研究发现最好尽可能减少一切背景噪声。

lines.t: Not everyone reacts in the same way to distractions.
lines.cn: 并非每个人对干扰的反应都相同。

lines.t: Other studies suggest some aspects of personality may make a difference.
lines.cn: 其他研究显示，某些人格特质可能造成差异。

lines.t: The researchers subjected shy, quiet people and confident, outgoing ones to high-arousal or low-arousal background music, general noise, or silence while asking them to remember words.
lines.cn: 研究者让害羞安静的人和自信外向的人在高唤醒或低唤醒的背景音乐、一般噪声或安静中记忆单词。

lines.t: Everyone performed best in the silent condition, but less sociable people were more negatively affected by each of the distractions.
lines.cn: 每个人在安静条件下表现最好，但不太善于交际的人受各种干扰的负面影响更大。

lines.t: So, when children are reading and trying to incorporate new material, parents could consider allowing some background music, particularly if it is instrumental and their child is the outgoing type.
lines.cn: 所以，当孩子在阅读并努力吸收新内容时，父母可以考虑允许放一些背景音乐，尤其是器乐，而且孩子属于外向型的话。
